newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends off for fourth day running.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends off for fourth day running.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed off at 479.25/480.25 per dollar for the fourth straight session as the Central Bank continued to keep back from trading, selling dollars into the market only towards the end of the day, brokers said.
"There's a lot of uncertainty in the market as to how the Central Bank is behaving," said one trader.
"It kept back right until the end of the day, when dollar demand sent the rate up to 480 ... only then did it sell dollars bringing the rate back down to its close," said one trader.
The Central Bank has assumed an uncharacteristic non- interventionist approach in recent sessions, apparently letting what many see as an increasingly overvalued bolivar gently slip.
But Central Bank director Carlos Hernandez Delfino told Reuters Thursday no change was currently seen for exchange rate policy.
That policy will continue to "promote a fall in inflation while also allowing a reasonable degree of flexibility that avoids market distortions and negative effects," he said.
Venezuela has followed a strong bolivar policy, where the unit ostensibly floats between exchange rate bands, to bear down on inflation since prices and exchange controls were removed last year.
Trade was brisk, brokers reported, with strong demand by corporate clients. The unit closed Wednesday at 479.00/480.00 per dollar.
